purpose: Nifedipine is used to treat high blood pressure and chest pain called angina. Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It can also help reduce how often you get chest pain episodes.
how_it_works: Your heart and blood vessels have tiny channels that let calcium in to cause tightening or squeezing. Nifedipine blocks those calcium channels so your blood vessels relax and widen. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and lowers your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: Flushing or feeling warm in your face, headache, dizziness, swollen ankles or feet, and feeling your heart beating fast or hard. You may also feel lightheaded when you stand up quickly. Most of these side effects tend to get better after your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not eat grapefruit or drink grapefruit juice while taking this medicine — it can raise the level of the drug in your body to unsafe levels. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this could worsen chest pain. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, heart failure, or are pregnant, since this medicine may not be safe in those situations.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for extended-release tablets is 30 to 60 mg taken once a day. Your doctor may increase it up to 90 or 120 mg per day if needed. Always swallow extended-release tablets whole — never crush, chew, or break them. Take it around the same time each day, with or without food.
